records.name: The Naked Stark
records.summary: A West Philadelphia modern dance company that makes close up, immersive dance shows and teaches movement classes and workshops, including an all-ages creative movement workshop.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a show, drop in to the weekly movement practice at Mascher Space, or take the Creative Movement Workshop, which is open to any level of dance experience. A fall Sunday class for ages 14 and up, aimed at intermediate and advanced movers, is also listed.

schedule.text: Weekly drop-in movement practice at Mascher Space. The day and time are not published on the site.

locations.label: Mascher Space Cooperative (weekly drop-in and Falling Up workshop)

cost.text: Show tickets are $5 to $50. The Creative Movement Workshop asks for a sliding scale of $5 to $25, and the group says cost should not stop anyone. Prices for the weekly drop-in and the fall Sunday class are not on the site.

requirements.gear: Wear long pants, or sleeves and knee pads, if you will move on the floor.

first_step.how: Email thenakedstark@gmail.com to ask when the Creative Movement Workshop dates are posted, since the site lists 2026 dates as coming soon.
first_step.basis: The Creative Movement Workshop says it is all levels and welcomes beginners, and the weekly drop-in is open to the public. The fall Sunday class is for intermediate and advanced movers, and the workshop dates are not yet posted, so the way in is not yet clear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Creative Movement Workshop is a series of four Sundays at The Cedar Works on Pentridge Street. It is open to all ages, with and without disabilities, and to people with no dance background. The site lists the space as ADA accessible and asks for a sliding scale of $5 to $25. The site does not say how long each session runs.
first_visit_tips: Wear long pants, or sleeves and knee pads, if you will be moving on the floor.
Ask by email for the session start time, since the site does not give one yet.
Pay what you can within the $5 to $25 sliding scale.

access.notes: The Creative Movement Workshop page lists its space as ADA accessible. Elevator and ASL details are not on the site.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass, 5 pages read. The Movement Practice page describes a fall Sunday class for ages 14 and up at intermediate to advanced level, which is separate from the weekly drop-in at Mascher Space; the drop-in day and time were not found. Dates for the Creative Movement Workshop are not yet posted. The Falling Up workshop (Dec 17 and 18, 10 am to 4 pm, $65 to $95 depending on registration date) and the Flood show are one-time items, so they are not in schedule; the Falling Up page gives no year. The contact page has no studio address or accessibility details.

records.name: The Philadelphia Chorus
records.summary: A community chorus founded in 1951 that holds auditions by appointment and is marking its 75th anniversary with a concert on December 5, 2026.
records.what_you_do: Book an audition by appointment, then sing with the chorus in Monday evening rehearsals and in its concerts. Singers must be 18 or older.

schedule.text: Rehearsals are on Monday evenings in University City.

locations.label: Rehearsals in University City (exact address not on the pages checked)

cost.text: The chorus site states no dues or fees, and the auditions page gives no audition fee.

first_step.how: Call 215-995-3118 or email thephiladelphiachorus@gmail.com to book an audition by appointment.
first_step.basis: Joining starts with an audition by appointment, which needs a booked slot and a sung test. The steps and contacts are published, so the way in is clear, but a newcomer cannot watch a rehearsal first.
first_step.what_to_expect: The audition asks you to sing scales and warm-ups and one song of your choice, and to sight-read a short excerpt. The site does not say how long it takes. Once you join, you rehearse on Monday evenings in University City and sing in concerts each season.
first_visit_tips: Choose a song you know well, and plan on accompaniment, which the chorus prefers.
When you book, ask how long the audition runs and where rehearsals meet, since the site does not say.
Do not come without booking, since auditions are by appointment only.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass. Rehearsal days now come from the chorus's own auditions page; tier 1 used a third-party listing. The exact rehearsal address, audition length and whether visitors can sit in on a rehearsal are not published. The Members Only area needs a login and was not opened. Batch lists kind club; the group file and the chorus's 990 filing point to nonprofit, so nonprofit is used here for a reviewer to confirm. The homepage names Raquel García as Artistic Director; the contact name kept here (Susan Shaman) comes from IRS records and was not contradicted. last_sign_of_life is the December 5, 2026 concert on the events page. A spring concert on April 10, 2027 at the same venue is also listed but not put in schedule because it is dated.

records.name: The Phoenix Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit community for people in recovery, the people who love them, and anyone who wants friends without alcohol or drugs. Its Philadelphia programs include workouts, art, social meetups and other free events.
records.what_you_do: Go to free sober activities led by volunteers, such as weekly chair yoga, weekly community yoga, fitness sessions, art, or social meetups. The listings checked have a Reserve Spot button. To volunteer, the site describes a short process that starts with its NewForm app and includes attending two events first. A sober community center is planned for North Philadelphia, with no opening date given.

schedule.text: Weekly chair yoga on Fridays at 10:30 am at Fox Chase Library, and weekly community yoga on Saturdays at 11 am, weather permitting. Other events are posted on the website.

locations.label: Other Philadelphia events (addresses not published on the pages checked)
Community yoga, weekly on Saturdays (in partnership with Historic Fairhill)

cost.text: The website says its programs are free. The yoga listings checked do not name a fee.

access.notes: The chair yoga listing is titled as chair based, but it gives no wheelchair, quiet space, parking or transit details.

first_step.how: Reserve a spot on the Friday chair yoga listing (Fox Chase Library, 10:30 am), or send a question through the Contact Us page on thephoenix.org.
first_step.basis: The site says people seeking connection are welcome, whether or not they are in recovery, and the Friday chair yoga is listed for all levels with a Reserve Spot button.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Friday chair yoga is 60 minutes, listed for all levels, with 15 spots per listing. The Saturday community yoga is a 60 minute gentle, slow flow class, and mats are provided. The site describes its activities as led by volunteers.
first_visit_tips: Reserve your spot on the listing first, since each class lists a limited number of places.
Check the listing before the Saturday class, since it is held weather permitting.
You do not need to bring a mat to the Saturday class, because the listing says mats are provided.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass. Two weekly yoga listings were read; neither gives a year or the start date of the series, so no dated evidence was added. The North Philadelphia sober community center is still described as planned with no opening date, and one search found no opening either, so it is not listed as open. The Contact Us page has a general form only, with no email or phone. A search snippet from a Meetup listing says Philadelphia programs need 48 hours of sobriety; it is not recorded, because Meetup is a lead only platform and the group's own pages do not say it. The partner names on the yoga listings are in leads_only with the listing URL, since no partner URL was given. The Trail Run listing has no detail, so it is not recorded.

records.name: The Plastic Club
records.summary: A volunteer-run art club in Center City that has supported artists since 1897. It runs weekly drawing and open studio sessions, monthly art shows, and film, music and poetry nights.
records.what_you_do: Drop in to a weekly drawing or open studio session. Where a fee is listed it is $5 to $10, and most sessions need no booking. You can also apply to join the club as a member: full membership is $60 a year, associate $40, and long distance $25. Artists can enter the club's exhibitions through its open calls.

schedule.text: Sessions run Monday to Saturday, mornings through evenings. Examples: Tuesday 9:30 am to 12:30 pm (clothed portrait model), Thursday 5:30 to 8:30 pm (life model), and Saturday 9:30 am to 12:30 pm (croquis). Printmaking open studio is on Saturdays from 10 am to 2 pm. A Tuesday night Zoom share is also listed.

cost.text: Life model and costume sessions are $10 each ($9 for members, $7 for students). Still life open studio is $5. Printmaking open studio is $10. Some sessions show no fee. Membership: full $60 a year, associate $40, long distance $25.

first_step.how: Read the Guide to Workshop Etiquette on the weekly workshops page, then come to a Thursday or Saturday open studio. New printmaking participants should text 609-682-1088 to book with the monitor first.
first_step.basis: Most workshops need no booking and are open to the public, though new people must read the etiquette guide first. Printmaking needs an appointment, and no beginner class is listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most life drawing sessions run about three hours with a model, and the club brings easels, drawing boards and small tables. The page does not say what to bring, so bring your own supplies if you have them. Printmaking is the one session that needs a booking first.
first_visit_tips: Read the Guide to Workshop Etiquette before you come, since every new participant is asked to.
Bring your own drawing supplies, since the page lists only easels, boards and tables from the club.
No pets are allowed in workshops, and the mask policy applies to indoor sessions.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass. The full weekly table is on the weekly workshops page; collage, clothed portrait, croquis and the Saturday afternoon long pose session show no fee there. The special workshops page is an empty placeholder. The membership page says full membership involves a board review of artwork and community involvement, and recommends taking part in club activities before applying. No accessibility information (stairs, elevator, wheelchair) appears on any page checked, so access is left out. No dated item was found, so status and last_sign_of_life are unchanged.

records.name: The Primavera Fund
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that mentors young musicians toward top music schools and careers, and helps students with the cost of study. It runs free career sessions for young musicians and keeps an instrument library.
records.what_you_do: Join one of the free virtual career sessions for young musicians, or ask about the Primavera Artist program. That program requires financial need and at least a year of playing your instrument, and the site does not say how to apply. Spring 2026 applications are closed, and the page does not say when the next round opens.

schedule.text: The group runs free virtual career sessions for young musicians, with a registration link posted on the homepage on the day of each one. Session times are not on the site.

locations.label: Mailing address (P.O. Box); sessions are virtual

cost.text: The career sessions are free. The site does not state a cost to artists in the mentoring program.

first_step.how: Watch the homepage for the link to the next free virtual career session, or email rachel@primaverafund.org to ask how to apply to the Primavera Artist program.
first_step.basis: The career sessions are free and open to young musicians, with a link posted for each one. The mentoring program has entry rules and no posted application steps, so it is not an easy first step.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each career session is virtual and free, with presentations from music professionals and time for questions. Session times are not on the site. The Primavera Artist program expects weekly private lessons, at least one weekly orchestra program and one smaller ensemble, at least two hours of practice a day, and summer music activities.
first_visit_tips: Know how long you have played your instrument, since the program asks for at least one year.
If you do not own an instrument, ask about the instrument library, since the site does not say who can borrow one.
Use the email on the site to ask about the application, since the steps are not posted.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass. The upcoming events page lists three March sessions with no year, so they are not recorded as dated items. The apply page says applications for the spring 2026 auditions are closed; no month is given, so last_sign_of_life is not set and status stays probably_active. Eligibility on the apply page: financial need (applicants review a cost of living estimate), at least one year of experience on the instrument, and enrollment in an extracurricular or after-school music program. The audition asks for a major scale and its relative minor, then a solo piece. The apply page gives no way to submit. The instrument library page describes donated instruments and gives no borrowing rules, so it is not cited. Mentoring age range and cost are not stated on any page checked.

records.name: The Print Center
records.summary: A free museum of printmaking and photography in Center City, founded in 1915. It shows changing exhibitions and runs a yearly competition for artists, and paid memberships bring member events and shop discounts.
records.what_you_do: Visit the free galleries during open hours, or book a guided tour, which the site offers for each exhibition and by appointment. Artists can enter The ANNUAL competition. Membership starts at $30 for students and $40 for artists, and the $50 individual level and up includes invitations to members-only events.

schedule.text: Open Tuesday to Saturday, 11 am to 6 pm, with free admission. Each exhibition has guided tours, and tours can also be booked by appointment.

cost.text: Admission is free. Memberships are optional, from $30 a year for students up to $500 for benefactors. The site does not give a fee for tours.

access.notes: The entry has a step of about 6 inches through a doorway about 31 inches wide. The second floor galleries are reached only by stairs. The first floor restroom is not wheelchair accessible. Seating is limited on both floors. Elevator, sensory options and ASL are not stated.

first_step.how: Come during open hours to see the free galleries, or call 215.735.6090 ext. 1 to book a guided tour by appointment.
first_step.basis: The galleries are free, open to the public, and need no sign-up. The site lists no beginner classes, and tours need a call to book by appointment.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is a walk through the current exhibition, with no sign-up and no admission fee. Listed exhibition tours run about 30 minutes, and the events page gives their times. If you use a wheelchair, plan around the entry step and the stairs to the second floor.
first_visit_tips: Parking: the museum points to the Academy House Parking Garage at 251 S. 15th Street, about one block away.
Expect limited seating on both floors.
Call 215.735.6090 ext. 1 if you need access details or tour times before you come.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass. The visit page says the museum was closed on Saturdays from August 1 to September 5, 2026; that closure has passed, so it is noted here and not in schedule. The events page lists public tours of the current exhibition on Oct 7 (passed), Oct 23 and Nov 13, 2026, all at set times; these one-off dates are not in schedule. The site does not state a fee or reservation rule for public tours. The appointment email is on the visit page but was not in the text returned. The homepage says some website content is temporarily unavailable. No SEPTA line or stop is named on the visit page, so none is recorded.

records.name: The Resource Exchange
records.summary: A reuse shop and gallery that sells donated and reclaimed art and craft materials at low prices. It runs workshops, a monthly gallery night and volunteer days, and gives artists a gallery call for work made from its materials.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a volunteer day through the sign-up link on the site, join a workshop such as the block printing session, or visit the shop and the gallery night. Artists can apply to the reCreate gallery, and the homepage lists a November 10 deadline for its open call.

schedule.text: The shop and gallery are open Wednesday to Saturday, 10 am to 6 pm, and Sunday, noon to 4 pm. The monthly gallery night is on the second Thursday, 5 to 8 pm.

cost.text: The site describes its shop items as affordable, and prices are not shown on the pages checked. Workshop, volunteer and gallery night costs are not listed on the site.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: Berks station on the Market-Frankford Line, per the contact page, which also names the 3 and 57 buses. Customer parking is free in the fenced lot. Step-free entry, elevator and wheelchair access are not stated.

first_step.how: Visit the shop at 1800 N. American St during open hours, or use the volunteer sign-up link on the site for the next volunteer day.
first_step.basis: Visitors are welcome in the shop and gallery with no sign-up, and volunteer days and workshops have sign-up links. The site does not give volunteer age limits or workshop costs.
first_step.what_to_expect: A shop visit is a browse through donated and reclaimed art and craft supplies, sold at low prices. The gallery shows work by local artists and makers who use reclaimed materials. Volunteer days and workshops have set times and sign-up links, but the site does not give a general shift length.
first_visit_tips: Free customer parking is in the fenced lot, and the shop sits on the right side toward the north end.
The shop is not listed as open on Monday or Tuesday, so plan for Wednesday to Sunday.
Ask about the cost of a workshop before you sign up, since the site does not show it.

records.notes: Tier 2 pass. The workshop and volunteer sign-up links go to Eventbrite, a lead only platform that was not followed, so workshop cost, age limits and volunteer tasks are not recorded. Tier 1's last_sign_of_life of 2026-10 rested on event dates whose year was inferred from the weekday; the page gives no year. It is replaced here with the January 14, 2026 impact post, which has a written date. The homepage lists a November 10 deadline for the reCreate open call, while the reCreate page says exhibitions rotate through the year; both are noted. The phone number 267.997.0060 comes from the contact page. The Oct 8 gallery night, Oct 17 block printing workshop and Oct 24 volunteer day are one-off dates and are not in schedule.

notes: All 7 groups in batch w21-tier2-deep-b were written as publish with research_tier 2. Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used; 34 WebFetch calls used (cap 60). No rate limiting seen; no bot checks or 403s. The one WebSearch found no opening date for The Phoenix's North Philadelphia center, so it stays planned. Two Resource Exchange links redirect to Eventbrite and were not followed. The Chorus Members Only page was not opened. Batch kind for The Philadelphia Chorus is club; the group file and the chorus's 990 filing point to nonprofit, so the record uses nonprofit for review. Partner venues and partners named on sites (Historic Fairhill, Yoga4philly, Mascher Space Cooperative, The Cedar Works) are in leads_only; none had a URL on the page, so none were checked. The four leads have no website URL on the pages read, and the single search was already spent, so they need a later pass with a URL or a search.
